title: Choose this year's replacements with a 0-1 model

expected.says: Run's report for the tiny fleet matches the expected report

blueprint.signature: def plan(fleet: list[Transformer], request: Request) -> Plan
blueprint.contract: Builds the model, solves it with HiGHS through MathOpt, and returns a Plan: each transformer whose variable is 1 mapped to FIRST_YEAR, the objective value, the dual bound, and the name of the termination reason as the status. With no plan found, a Plan with no replacements and the status alone. Nothing the solver prints may reach standard output, since Run's report is compared line by line.
blueprint.idea: Read the termination first, then the variable values; a binary is 1 when its value is above 0.5.

lesson.title: 4.2.2 Reading `SolveResult`: Termination, Primal and Dual Solutions, Statistics

blueprint.signature: def build(fleet: list[Transformer], request: Request) -> Built
blueprint.contract: A new module. Returns a Built, a dataclass holding the MathOpt model, the variables `x` keyed by transformer id, and the budget row: one binary variable per transformer named `x_<tid>`, one row named `budget` keeping the summed cost of the replaced units within request.budget, and the summed risk of the replaced units as the objective to maximize.
blueprint.idea: A yes-or-no choice per unit under one budget is a 0-1 knapsack: the best list is a combination, which no ranking finds in general.

blueprint.signature: def feasible(fleet: list[Transformer], request: Request, replace: dict[str, int]) -> bool
blueprint.contract: Builds the same model, fixes the variable of every listed unit to 1 and of every other unit to 0, solves, and answers whether the solver found a plan.
blueprint.idea: To test a rule, pin a whole plan with variable bounds and ask whether it is feasible; a pair of plans on either side of a limit shows the row is there and in the right place.

lesson.title: 12.3.1 Unit-Testing One Constraint at a Time

cases: the plan takes the units with the most risk, not the worst condition scores
the plan uses money a ranking leaves unspent when it stops at a unit that does not fit
the plan removes as much risk as the best subset within the budget
the model allows a list that spends exactly the budget and refuses one just over it
